title: 2016 AMC 8
copyright: Problems: Mathematical Association of America, American Mathematics Competitions.

questions.stem: The longest professional tennis match lasted a total of $11$ hours and $5$ minutes. How many minutes is that?
questions.solution:
Convert the 11 hours into minutes, then include the remaining 5 minutes:

$$11\times60+5=665.$$

The published result is 665 minutes.

questions.stem: In rectangle $ABCD,$ $AB=6$ and $AD=8.$ Point $M$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AD}.$ What is the area of $\triangle AMC?$
questions.solution:
The midpoint condition gives $AM=8/2=4$. Taking $AM$ as the triangle's base, its perpendicular height from $C$ is $6$. Therefore,

$$[AMC]=\frac12\times4\times6=12.$$

questions.stem: Four students take an exam. Three of their scores are $70,$ $80,$ and $90.$ If the average of their four scores is $70,$ then what is the remaining score?
questions.solution:
An average of 70 for four students requires a combined score of $4\times70=280$. Remove the three given scores:

$$280-(70+80+90)=40.$$

questions.stem: When Cheenu was a boy he could run $15$ miles in $3$ hours and $30$ minutes. As an old man he can now walk $10$ miles in $4$ hours. How many minutes longer does it take for him to travel a mile now compared to when he was a boy?
questions.solution: Express both paces in minutes per mile. The childhood pace is $(3\times60+30)/15=14$. The later walking pace is $(4\times60)/10=24$. Their difference is $24-14=10$ minutes per mile.

questions.stem:
The number $N$ is a two-digit number with the following properties:
  • When $N$ is divided by $9,$ the remainder is $1.$
  • When $N$ is divided by $10,$ the remainder is $3.$
What is the remainder when $N$ is divided by $11?$
questions.solution: The remainder modulo 10 restricts the candidates to $13,23,33,43,53,63,73,83,93$. The source identifies $73$ as the only candidate satisfying the remainder condition modulo 9. Since $73=6\times11+7$, the requested remainder is 7.

questions.stem:
The following bar graph represents the length (in letters) of the names of $19$ people. What is the median length of these names?

![Problem diagram](assets/6.svg)
questions.solution: For 19 ordered observations, the median occupies position 10. Accumulating the frequencies in the supplied graph places the tenth name in the four-letter group. Hence the median is 4 letters.

questions.stem: Which of the following numbers is not a perfect square?
questions.solution: Options A, C, and E have even exponents and therefore represent squares. Option D also represents a square because its base, 4, is already a square. The remaining choice is $2^{2017}$, option B.

questions.stem: Find the value of the expression $$ \begin{gathered} 100 - 98 + 96 - 94 + 92 - 90 \\ {}+ \cdots + 8 - 6 + 4 - 2. \end{gathered} $$
questions.solution:
Pair successive terms:

$$(100-98)+(96-94)+\cdots+(4-2).$$

The source counts 25 pairs, each contributing 2. Thus the expression equals $25\times2=50$.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the distinct prime integer divisors of $2016?$
questions.solution:
The published prime factorization is

$$2016=2^5\times3^2\times7.$$

Count each prime only once: $2+3+7=12$.

questions.stem: Suppose that $a \ast b$ means $3a - b.$ What is the value of $x$ if $$2 \ast (5 \ast x) = 1?$$
questions.solution: Apply the custom operation first to the inner expression: $5\ast x=15-x$. The outer expression becomes $6-(15-x)=x-9$. Consequently $x-9=1$, giving $x=10$.

questions.stem:
Determine how many two-digit numbers satisfy the following property:

When the number is added to the number obtained by reversing its digits, the sum is $132.$
questions.solution:
Writing the digits as $a,b$, the required sum becomes

$$(10a+b)+(10b+a)=11(a+b)=132.$$

Thus $a+b=12$. The source lists $(3,9),(4,8),(5,7),(6,6),(7,5),(8,4),(9,3)$, yielding seven qualifying numbers.

questions.stem: Jefferson Middle School has the same number of boys and girls. Three-fourths of the girls and two-thirds of the boys went on a field trip. What fraction of the students on the field trip were girls?
questions.solution:
Use the source's convenient model of 12 students of each sex. The trip then includes 9 girls and 8 boys. The required share is

$$\frac{9}{9+8}=\frac9{17}.$$

questions.stem: Two different numbers are randomly selected from the set $$\{ - 2, -1, 0, 3, 4, 5\}$$ and multiplied together. What is the probability that the product is $0?$
questions.solution: There are $\binom62=15$ unordered selections. A zero product requires choosing 0 together with one of the five other entries, giving five favorable selections. Therefore the probability is $5/15=1/3$.

questions.stem:
Karl’s car uses a gallon of gas every $35$ miles, and his gas tank holds $14$ gallons when it is full.

One day, Karl started with a full tank of gas, drove $350$ miles, bought $8$ gallons of gas, and continued driving to his destination. When he arrived, his gas tank was half full. How many miles did Karl drive that day?
questions.solution: The initial 350 miles consume $350/35=10$ gallons, leaving 4. Buying 8 gallons raises the supply to 12. Finishing with 7 gallons means another 5 gallons were consumed, covering $5\times35=175$ miles. Total travel is $350+175=525$ miles.

questions.stem: What is the largest power of $2$ that is a divisor of $13^4 - 11^4?$
questions.solution:
Use the source's difference-of-squares factorization:

$$13^4-11^4=(13^2+11^2)(13^2-11^2)=290\times48=32\times435.$$

The factor 435 is odd, so the full power of 2 dividing the expression is 32.

questions.stem: Annie and Bonnie are running laps around a $400$-meter oval track. They started together, but Annie has pulled ahead, because she runs $25\%$ faster than Bonnie. How many laps will Annie have run when she first passes Bonnie?
questions.solution: In the time Bonnie completes one lap, Annie completes $1\frac14$ laps. Each Bonnie lap therefore gives Annie a quarter-lap lead. A full-lap lead occurs after Bonnie's fourth lap, when Annie has completed five laps.

questions.stem: An ATM password at Fred’s Bank is composed of four digits from $0$ to $9,$ with repeated digits allowable. If no password may begin with the sequence $9,$ $1,$ $1,$ then how many passwords are possible?
questions.solution: Allowing repetition and initial zeroes gives $10^4$ four-character passwords. The excluded prefix fixes three positions, leaving ten possibilities for the final digit. Subtracting these gives $10^4-10=9990$.

questions.stem:
In an All-Area track meet, $216$ sprinters enter a $100$-meter dash competition. The track has $6$ lanes, so only $6$ sprinters can compete at a time. At the end of each race, the five non-winners are eliminated, and the winner will compete again in a later race.

How many races are needed to determine the champion sprinter?
questions.solution:
One champion remains only after 215 competitors have been removed. Each race removes five sprinters, so the source obtains

$$\frac{215}{5}=43\text{ races}.$$

questions.stem: The sum of $25$ consecutive even integers is $10{,}000.$ What is the largest of these $25$ consecutive even integers?
questions.solution: The middle integer equals the average, $10000/25=400$. Twelve increments of size 2 separate it from the largest integer. Hence the largest is $400+12\times2=424$.

questions.stem: The least common multiple of $a$ and $b$ is $12,$ and the least common multiple of $b$ and $c$ is $15.$ What is the least possible value of the least common multiple of $a$ and $c?$
questions.solution: Because $b$ divides both 12 and 15, the source considers $b=1$ and $b=3$. The first case forces $a=12,c=15$, giving least common multiple 60. In the second case, $a=4,c=5$ attain 20. The smaller possible result is 20.

questions.stem: A top hat contains $3$ red chips and $2$ green chips. Chips are drawn randomly, one at a time without replacement, until all $3$ of the reds are drawn or until both green chips are drawn. What is the probability that the $3$ reds are drawn?
questions.solution: Imagine completing the entire random ordering of chips. Red is exhausted first exactly when the final chip is green. Of the $\binom52=10$ possible green-position pairs, four include the final position. Thus the desired probability is $4/10=2/5$.

questions.stem:
Rectangle $DEFA$ below is a $3 \times 4$ rectangle with $DC=CB=BA=1.$ The area of the “bat wings” (shaded area) is

![Problem diagram](assets/22.svg)
questions.solution:
Follow the labels in the source diagram: $I$ and $G$ are the midpoints of $AD$ and $EF$, and $H=CF\cap BE$.

![Published solution diagram for Problem 22](assets/22sol.svg)

Triangle $BCE$ has area $\frac12(1)(4)=2$. Similar triangles $BCH$ and $EFH$ have base ratio $1:3$, so their heights satisfy $IH:HG=1:3$. As $IG=4$, this gives $IH=1$. Thus $[BCH]=\frac12$, and one shaded wing has area $[ECH]=2-\frac12=\frac32$. Doubling for the symmetric wing gives area 3.

questions.stem:
Two congruent circles centered at points $A$ and $B$ each pass through the other circle’s center. The line containing both $A$ and $B$ is extended to intersect the circles at points $C$ and $D.$

The circles intersect at two points, one of which is $E.$ What is the degree measure of $\angle CED?$
questions.solution:
Use the labeling of the published diagram below.

![Published solution diagram for Problem 23](assets/23.svg)

The radii $AE,EB,AB$ are equal, so triangle $AEB$ is equilateral and $\angle AEB=60^\circ$. Since $DB$ and $AC$ are diameters, their angles at $E$ are right angles. The source combines these as

$$\angle CED=\angle DEB+\angle AEC-\angle AEB=90^\circ+90^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ.$$

questions.stem: The digits $1,$ $2,$ $3,$ $4,$ and $5$ are each used once to write a five-digit number $PQRST.$ The three-digit number $PQR$ is divisible by $4,$ the three-digit number $QRS$ is divisible by $5,$ and the three-digit number $RST$ is divisible by $3.$ What is $P?$
questions.solution: Divisibility of $QRS$ by 5 fixes $S=5$. The source lists $QR=12,24,32$ as the possibilities imposed by divisibility of $PQR$ by 4. For $QR=12$ or $32$, no unused digit $T$ makes $25T$ divisible by 3. Thus $QR=24$; then $45T$ requires $T=3$. The remaining digit is $P=1$, producing $12453$.

questions.stem:
A semicircle is inscribed in an isosceles triangle with base $16$ and height $15$ so that the diameter of the semicircle is contained in the base of the triangle as shown. What is the radius of the semicircle?

![Problem diagram](assets/25.svg)
questions.solution:
Follow the source diagram, where $O$ bisects the base and $OE$ is the radius to the point of tangency.

![Published solution diagram for Problem 25](assets/25sol.svg)

The right half-triangle has legs 8 and 15, so its hypotenuse $BC$ is 17. Its area is $\frac12(8)(15)=60$. As $OE\perp BC$, the same area is $\frac12(17)(OE)$. Consequently the radius is $OE=120/17$.
